## Scenario

**Redistributing data:**
Bioconductor passes on reference annotations and experimental data.
Which RDM standard or practice would make the most difference if it adopted it?

## Load R packages


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ExperimentHub))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(AnnotationHub))
```
:::

### Exported to a CSV file

Bioconductor only provides a SQLite file that contains metadata about the datasets available.

Users are expected to interact with it via R functions provided by the *ExperimentHub* and *AnnotationHub* packages.

The code below exports that table of metadata to a CSV file that you can download and browse in Excel.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
edata <- as.data.frame(S4Vectors::mcols(ehub))

if (!dir.exists("03-redistributing-data"))
    dir.create("03-redistributing-data")

write.csv(edata, "03-redistributing-data/ExperimentHub_metadata.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```
:::


Download the output CSV file [here](03-redistributing-data/ExperimentHub_metadata.csv)
